content: Demeclocycline is a medication that should be taken as directed by your healthcare provider. The dosage depends on your specific medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal effectiveness, it is important to take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. If your condition persists or worsens, inform your doctor promptly. Common side effects of demeclocycline may include diarrhea, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or rectal discomfort. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. This risk is higher in women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of IH. If IH develops, it typically resolves after stopping the medication, but there is a possibility of permanent vision loss or blindness. In rare cases, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. diff). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of demeclocycline may also result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking demeclocycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other tetracycline medications (such as doxycycline, minocycline, or tetracycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Demeclocycline may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, demeclocycline can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Demeclocycline should not be used in children under 8 years of age, as it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other problems. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using demeclocycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Demeclocycline may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as some urine tests for sugar, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses on demeclocycline and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated demeclocycline can result in serious illness. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. If you are using demeclocycline for long-term treatment or to manage SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion), regular laboratory and medical tests (such as complete blood count, kidney and liver function, and mineral levels) should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
